including a character only known as 'Hot Girl' - as she's set to return to acting after eight years The Duchess of Sussex is to return to acting in the film Close Personal Friends READ MORE: Oprah gives brazen shoutout to Meghan Markle in new gift guide By MELODY FLETCHER Published: 04:55 EST, 7 November 2025 | Updated: 05:02 EST, 7 November 2025 e-mail 86 shares 532 View comments Meghan Markle is set to make a return to the world of acting, eight years after she quit the industry. The Duchess of Sussex , 44, is said to have been 'swamped with offers' for her return to the limelight, and will be playing herself in the film Close Personal Friends, with filming taking place in Pasadena in LA. But before she married Prince Harry and joined the royal family , Meghan's acting career looked very different - consisting mainly of bit parts and cameos in largely forgettable and poorly reviewed movies - and she was not nearly so in demand. Before making her name as Rachel Zane in the TV show Suits, Meghan secured minor Hollywood roles in Horrible Bosses (2011) and Remember Me (2010) - where she was typecast as a 'cute' or 'hot girl', with only seconds of screentime . Often, her cameo and pilot roles, such as her brief appearance kissing Russell Brand in Get Him To The Greek (2010) and The Boys And Girls Guide To Getting Down (2011), never actually ended up making the final cut. As a result, the now-Duchess was forced to resort to a series of raunchy roles - and was seen parading around in sexy negligee for the majority of her feature in 2012's Random Encounters - not to mention her explicit scene in the 90210 TV series . Critics, meanwhile, were less than impressed with the final results, even warning viewers that Meghan's 2006 film Deceit would 'bore them to death'. When she finally did score leading roles towards the end of her acting career, Meghan was mainly seen in repetitive and unchallenging Hallmark Movies, receiving mixed reviews at best. The mother-of-two previously told how she would get plenty of auditions but was regularly rejected by directors - which was a 'lot to chip away at your self-esteem'. Here, we give a rundown of all Meghan's film roles before meeting Prince Harry - most of which you probably won't have heard of... A Lot Like Love (2005) Meghan made her film debut in 2005, playing Natalie, the 'Hot Girl' in A Lot Like Love Meghan, then aged 24 and an unknown actress, made her big screen debut alongside Hollywood heartthrob Ashton Kutcher in the 2005 film called A Lot Like Love , where she was famously credited as 'Hot Girl.' The Duchess' very first film role was a total flop at the box office but Meghan herself, wearing a bright pink top, was only on screen for 31 seconds, and saw her attempting to flirt with Kutcher's internet entrepreneur character Oliver Martin on a flight. But she was left stunned when Oliver showed no interest because of his complicated on-off relationship with photographer Emily Friehl, Alias actress Amanda Peet. And she ended up being chatted up by business partner Jetter played by actor Kal Penn instead, who was sat across the aisle. Although she introduced herself as Natalie, she only appeared in the credits as 'Hot Girl.' The film was like an American version of One Day, where a couple met regularly over a seven-year period before falling in love. The moment was featured in Harry and Meghan's Netflix docu-series as they discussed Meghan's film career. The film received mixed reviews and a score of 40 per cent on Rotten Tomatoes, while one review in the Observer called it 'neither bad nor good enough to be anything other than utterly forgettable'. Deceit (2006) Meghan played Gwen in 2006's Deceit, again another small role for the budding actress In her second film role, Meghan again landed only a small part, playing a girl-next-door called Gwen, again appearing only in one scene. Over the kitchen table, Meghan's characeter dispensed unwanted advice to a friend caught up in a murder mystery. Her handy advice included lines such as: 'You're an investigative journalist; do what you do best - investigate her' The psychological thriller, released in 2006, followed a young man returning home after his father's death and falling in love with his best friend's wife. It explored attraction, violence, and deception. Meghan played Gwen in one scene in the film, a friend of the protagonist who offered advice to the main character. Director Matthew Cole Weiss previously revealed he'd met Prince Harry, who told him he had watched the film. The film has poor reviews online, scoring just 4.5/10 on IMDB, with viewers saying it has 'weak acting,' 'no characters' adding it will 'bore you to death'. Remember Me (2010) The Duchess did score some Hollywood roles in her film acting career, starring in Remember Me alongside Robert Pattinson In Remember Me, starring Robert Pattinson and Emilie de Ravin, Meghan had a small role as a bartender, who was aptly named Megan. She briefly interacted with Pattinson's character and only had one, three-word line: 'Do not speak', when she told his friend not to chat with her. On working with the Twilight star, Meghan recalled: 'He's a really lovely guy and a really great example to be able to watch someone who is young, who's stardom has really taken over his live in such a huge way, and yet he's still gracious, humble and cool. I think that is really endearing.' This movie marked Robert Pattinson's departure from his Twilight fame, so it would be easy to forget that a future star had a small role in the same production as well. The movie follows the story of Tyler Hawkins, who falls in love with Amy, played by Emilie de Ravin, but dies in the Twin Towers on 9/11/2001. The rom com was a financial success, grossing $56million worldwide. However, it fared less well with critics, only scoring 26 per cent on Rotten Tomatoes. The twist at the end of the show - that Pattinson's character is in his father's office in the World Trade Centre when the 9/11 attacks take place - was branded 'shockingly offensive' by Rolling Stone, and 'exploitative' by other reviewers. Meghan's real life ex-husband Trevor Engelson, was one of the film's producers, and the pair tied the knot a year later, during a party-filled celebration in Jamaica in 2011. They eventually divorced in 2014, with Meghan being linked to several men during her single years before she met now-husband Prince Harry in 2016. Get Him To The Greek (2010) Meghan Markle played Tatiana in comedy Get Him To The Greek, in which she's seen kissing comedian Russell Brand Meghan Markle played Tatiana in comedy Get Him To The Greek, in which she's seen kissing comedian Russell Brand. She reportedly had a 40-second role as a girl in a strapless metallic dress and snogged Brand's character. However, Meghan was never given a credit in the film and the scene never made it to the final cut. Is this really her? Everyone, including royal biographer Andrew Morton, says yes, reported the Mail's Jan Moir . The plot followed a record company employee, played by Jonah Hill, who went to London to get an eccentric English rock star (Russell Brand) to the Greek Theatre in Los Angeles. However, Snow is a party animal and took them on a wild ride involving alcohol and women, meeting Meghan Markle along the way. Speaking to the Evening Standard, Russell Brand said: 'She [Meghan] was in a film that I did, Get Him To The Greek it was called. 'I don't remember the film that much but I think I planted one on her. Scripted in the scene. I only know this because I think I saw a clip of it somewhere. 'They should bring that up [at the wedding]... if anyone has any reason... yeah Russell Brand snogged her in the film!' He said he didn't realise she was in it at the time as she 'wasn't married to a royal person'. The film was not panned by critics and was even said to have had its 'moments' - though Meghan's role was too short to appear in any of them. Horrible Bosses (2011) Horrible Bosses continued the trend of Meghan playing bit parts in Hollywood dark comedies Horrible Bosses in 2011 saw Meghan star alongside Jennifer Aniston and Jason Sudeikis. However, it seemed to continue the trend of her playing bit parts in Hollywood dark comedies, again having only a short cameo. The movie told the story of three employees who conspired to kill their overbearing employers. Meghan played courier driver Jamie in the comedy film and shared a few lines with Sudeikis' Kurt Buckman in another 30-second scene. In her scene, Jason Sudeikis chatted her up, saying: 'You're too cute to be a FedEx girl. You've got to be an actress or a model or something.' Her small role in the movie resurfaced after her relationship with Prince Harry became public. The film was surprisingly successful, but Meghan's role didn't attract any noticeable attention at the time. The Boys and Girls Guide to Getting Down (2011) Meghan Markle played Dana in the pilot to The Boys And Girls Guide To Getting Down, which never went anywhere Meghan Markle played Dana in The Boys And Girls Guide To Getting Down, which followed a group of friends on a night out in Los Angeles. The movie is described in the trailer as 'a film about sex drugs, booze and all around bad behaviour.' Filmed in 2011, and directed by Michael Shapiro, Meghan's character worked as a guide to Californian party-lovers, advising them on what to do and what not to do on a night out. The tongue-in-cheek movie touched on a lot of raunchy subjects, including drugs, sex and alcohol. Meghan's character Dana was seen snorting cocaine, wearing a tight black dress and obsessing about getting a boob job. The TV movie, described as a 'real life guide to sexy, drugs, and bad behavior', was filmed prior to Meghan landing her role on Suits and never went anywhere. According to IMDB, the pilot 'takes you through a night of partying in L.A.' It is described as 'funny' and 'somewhat outrageous' while offering advice to viewers on the ins and outs of partying. '[The film] gives partiers helpful tips about which substances should not be mixed, how to approach potential hook-ups, avoid undesirables [and] basically have a good time without completely destroying yourself,' the plot read on IMDB. The Candidate (2011) The Candidate, 2011: Meghan pulls strings to get a role in this hard-boiled sci-fi short film — which was produced by her then-husband, Trevor Engelson Sci-fi short film The Candidate (2011) was also produced by Meghan's then-husband, Trevor Engelson. The role was again a brief one, with Meghan starring in two scenes as Kat the secretary whose boss, Burton Grunzer, wanted to kill his incompetent colleague, Whitman Hayes. Meghan's character read her boss a latter from someone called Carl Tucker, whose text messages he repeatedly ignored. The film, by David Karlak, itself is only 19 minutes long, but received a positive reaction at the time, with one person saying it was 'better than most thrillers I've seen in theaters'. A description on the American Film Institute website reads: 'An underhanded company man is offered assistance by a secret organization that immerses him in forces beyond his control.' Dysfunctional Friends (2012) Meghan played photographer Terry in 2012's low budget film, 'Dysfunctional Friends' In the low budget film 'Dysfunctional Friends', Meghan showed she also has experience on the other side of the camera. Playing glamorous photographer Terry, Markle was seen in the little-known film shooting a handsome underwear model in a scene in scene focusing on his manhood. With flowing locks and wearing a black vest with off-the-shoulder baggy shirt, a no-nonsense Terry told male model Stylz, played by Christian Keyes: 'This is not porn. It's for the Sunday papers. This situation you have going on, it's got to get tucked in.' The images, for an underwear campaign, saw Markle's character getting increasingly frustrated with how her model was sat, before finally raging at him: 'Tuck it in!' The film followed nine friends who went their different ways after finishing college before reuniting at a rich friend's funeral. They find out that they will be eligible for a big inheritance if they stay at his mansion for five days. It bombed at the box office but paved the way for Markle to take on more serious roles. Keyes later told People Magazine that he had been 'slapped' by the 'future Queen' during filming. He explained: '[Meghan] said, 'I might improv an extra smack,' and I was like, 'smack away!' 'I knew she was going to put a little hand on it. She had some torque and rotation in the wrist.' 'It was one of her first acting gigs and she has [acting] chops, she had them back then. She was great on set. She was super cool and approachable. She was a class act.' Random Encounters (2013) Meghan had another racy role in Random Encounters, playing party girl Mindy Filmed over 18 days in 2010, the low budget romantic comedy was set in the showbusiness community in Los Angeles In Random Encounters, Meghan played Mindy, a party girl who brings home a different guy every night, and the best friend of singleton Laura, who strikes up a romance with Kevin, a man she met in a coffee shop. Filmed over 18 days in 2010, the low budget romantic comedy was set in the showbusiness community in Los Angeles. During the chick flick, which was made pre-Suits before being re-released, Mindy popped up in a host of revealing outfits including a sexy negligee before seducing a male co-star and sleeping with a cop who stopped her for a traffic offence. In one scene, Mindy could be seen showing her friend the ropes on 'the biggest dating site in LA'. She also revealed her top tips for catching a man's eye in a night club: 'Look like you're really bored and have a serious attitude problem.' When her frustrated single friend moaned that she is 'chasing a guy who doesn't insist,' Mindy replied: 'Oh honey, aren't we all.' 'It just goes to show, you just have to be in the right place at the right time. Sometimes, you only get one shot.' In one particularly racy scene Meghan was seen undressing actor Michael Rady as her character tried to make a move in a dimly-lit apartment. At other points in the film, Meghan flitted across the screen in flirty summer dresses and party frocks. Director Boris Undorf later spoke about Markle's can-do attitude while filming, reflecting: 'All the comforts of a bigger project weren't there. 'She was very much like, 'Yep, I got it. I know it's long hours, but I love doing it, and I'll do my best' to serve the film, not just myself.'' Co-star Abby Wathen (Laura) added: 'It was great to work with Meghan because she's a pro, and it's great to work with pros... It was lovely. We sat in my trailer and just giggled. She's just vivacious.' In 2018, the budget rom com was released in the UK for the first time - just two weeks before Meghan married Prince Harry. When Sparks Fly (2014) In 2014, Meghan finally landed her first major film role in Hallmark movie, When Sparks Fly Meghan's character Amy finds there's no place like how when she reunited with her high school sweetheart In 2014, Meghan finally landed a major film role, playing the lead role in the Hallmark movie, When Sparks Fly. She played Amy Peterson, a journalist who quits her small town for the big city of Chicago. She then returned to her hometown to write a human interest story about Independence Day weekend. Amy discovered that there's no place like home - and no boy like her high school sweetheart. Meghan said at the time: 'I wanted to do a romantic comedy. When the script came in, it was exactly the kind of project I wanted to be part of. 'It was light and easy and it was a departure from Rachel [Suits], who is so refined and polished. Amy Peterson is very opposite and closer to my true personality. 'It was fun to eat ribs and get barbecue sauce all over my face and run around in jeans all day.' Hallmark films all generally follow the same plot points, and while they make for comforting watching, are generally not considered 'challenging' acting roles. In 2021 alone, the channel made 41 Christmas films, with each film relatively low budget and without famous names. Anti-Social (2015) Meghan - then 35 - played American fashion model Kirsten who falls in love with Dee (Gregg Sulkin) in Anti-Social Following her relationship with Prince Harry, the film was re-released and re-edited to give Meghan a bigger role Set in England and filmed largely in Hungary, Anti-Social followed a successful street artist who was forced to jeopardise his future to help his criminal brother when gang rivalry escalates. The gangland war turned their lives upside down, bringing the attention of the police as well as other criminals. The low-budget British coming-of-age story was inspired by a number of real-life smash-and-grab raids across London from 2009 to 2013. Again, the Duchess was chosen to play the female lead and it even co-starred grime star Skepta. Meghan - then 35 - played American fashion model Kirsten who falls in love with Dee (Gregg Sulkin), a talented Banksy-esque street-artist who was sucked into crime. One of her lines included: 'I know you have had to climb a mountain to get away from this crap and see life for what it can be. You inspire me.' Following her relationship with Prince Harry, the film was re-released and re-edited to give Meghan a bigger role as bosses sought to capitalise on her new royal links. Originally, it had been shown at just 40 screens in the UK when it was released in 2015. Speaking of the decision to re-release it, Director Reg Traviss - who had dated Amy Winehouse before she died - said he wanted to 'delve deeper into one of the storylines with.. a shorter, more compact version of the original'. In the three-minute trailer, Meghan's character was shown modelling perfume, emerging from a shower and drinking champagne at a number of West End nightclubs. She was heard saying: 'I'm going to go and see my boyfriend, he's an artist. A street artist.' In a scene which showed shoot-outs in London, depicting Marcus and his cool friends getting pulled into a dangerous gang war, she said: 'I hate violence... I'm from a sleepy little beach town, I'm just not used to this.' Upon its release, the film generally received negative reviews, with one critic calling the film a 'painful slog'. In The Observer, critic Mark Kermode awarded it two stars, calling it an 'uninspiring crime caper' that 'sits awkwardly alongside dreary discussions of the politics of street art'. Dater's Handbook (2016) Meghan's final film role saw her play Cassandra Barber in 2016's Dater's Handbook Cass soon realised that there was no rule book to love, binned her manual and met the man of her dreams In Meghan's final film role before quitting the industry upon joining the Royal Family, she played another lead role for the Hallmark Channel, in 2016's Dater's Handbook. The romantic movie centred around Cassandra Barber, who realised she had a recurring habit of picking the wrong type of guy, turning to relationship expert, Dr. Susie, and her latest self-help book, The Dater's Handbook to help with her ailing love life. 'Of course I wanna get married,' Meghan's character Cass told her mother. 'I've got to change how I choose relationships.' She followed the advice in Dr. Susie's book to evaluate potential suitors, and was forced to choose between reliable George (Jonathan Scarfe) and fun-loving Robert (Kristoffer Polaha). Cass soon realised that there was no rule book to love, binned her manual and met the man of her dreams. Little did Meghan know that six months later she'd meet her real-life prince. Successful career women, both Cassandra and Meghan were set up with their dream suitor by a mutual pal, bonding on and off-screen with their respective suitors over their shared love of animals and the great outdoors. Additionally, Meghan and her character were whisked away on sporty dates by their suitors - while Cass' mother joined the pair at a concert in the movie, Harry flew Meghan's mother Doria to the Invictus Games in Toronto in real life. Many joked at the time of the movie's release that while the character she played on screen had been unlucky in love, Meghan's real love life was very different. During the film's press tour, Meghan said: 'At the end of the day, when it comes down to finding the person that you're right for, that's not the person you're going to play games with. 'I think following her heart has really ended up proving to work out well for Cass, and I think for a lot of women watching this, I would give them that same advice.' The film, a classic Hallmark movie, was branded 'predictable and simple' by critics. On IMDB, one reviewer even said: 'The story was silly, the acting was below average, and the actors had no chemistry.' And when outside gets cold, there's no place I'd rather be than inside somewhere, under a blanket and curled up with a book, or on the couch watching a good movie. Heck, it doesn't even need to be a good movie. A bad movie will do just fine if it's the kind of bad movie that's also kind of great . Part of me wants to tell you that I'm not here to try to defend Roland Emmerich's 2009 disaster movie , 2012 , with its overflowing cast of characters, fairly convoluted plot, and extremely long runtime (two and a half hours?!). Its 40% Critic score on Rotten Tomatoes seems fair to me, and the audience score isn't much better. I can't defend the ratings, but I still like watching this movie. Like every two years or so, I get a hankering for it, the same way I do some other disaster movies I can't really defend . Honestly, when I recently saw that 2012 was streaming for free, I knew the odds were high that I already owned this movie on digital at some point. And I did, so I'm set, but if you want to revisit this movie and you haven't already secured your own copy on home video, as of this writing, you can watch it for free with ads on Tubi. All you need to know going in is that this is an apocalyptic situation that's affecting the whole world. And as you'll see in the first two-thirds of the film, major catastrophes unfold, from earthquakes to volcanic eruptions and all sorts of other nightmarish scenarios as a result of these natural disasters. I'm going to be vague at this point, because it is quite suspenseful if you haven't seen it, but this is one of those disaster movies where there's a secret place only a small percentage of the earth's population is aware of or allowed to go to in order to survive the end of the world, and our heroes (and some not-so-heroes) are trying to get there. (Image credit: Sony Pictures) Oh Yeah, And The Cast Is Fire The cast for this movie is great. The main characters include Jackson Curtis ( John Cusack ), an author and father trying to protect his family, including his kids and his ex-wife (played by Amanda Peet). Oliver Platt plays the White House Chief of Staff, while Danny Glover plays the President and father to Thandiwe Newton's character, Laura Wilson. As I mentioned, Woody Harrelson makes an appearance as a science conspiracy guy who's not entirely wrong about the ideas he's raving about, while Chiwetel Ejiofor plays the actual scientist who advises the president. (Image credit: Sony Pictures) 2012 Isn't Perfect, But It Also Never Lets Me Down Here's the thing. I do think Roland Emmerich (who co-wrote the film, in addition to directing) made a solid effort to try to make something more out of your standard disaster movie. There's just a lot going on in the film and with so many different characters brought in and out amidst what's happening with the main characters, it's kind of hard to feel invested in anything as much as I think I'm supposed to. I always find myself wishing I felt more about the characters and story by the end of the movie than I do, but it's not so bad that I regret watching it in the first place (and not so bad that I know I'll want to watch it again at some point in the future). The American Horror Story actress, 50, will be honoured in a ceremony on Tuesday 2 December, becoming the 2,829th star on the legendary Los Angeles walk. A star of stage and screen, Paulson is being recognised in the television category. The other categories are motion pictures, recording, radio, live performances and sports entertainment. It’s especially meaningful that her star is located right next to that of her friend and longtime collaborator, Ryan Murphy. Reactions on social media all essentially said the same thing, with one person tweeting: ‘Took them long enough but finally’, and another calling it a “long-overdue honour.” Sarah Paulson and Holland Taylor have been together since 2015. She’s earned two Critics’ Choice Awards and five Emmy nominations over those seasons. Furthermore, she’s returning for season 13. While she has been more recently seen in the panned series , All’s Fair , Paulson has had starring roles in series such as Ratched (for which she was nominated for a Golden Globe), Mr. & Mrs. Smith (for which she earned her ninth Emmy Award nomination), The Bear , and many more. Paulson won her first Emmy in the Outstanding Lead Actress in a Miniseries or Movie category for her role Marcia Clark in The People v. O.J. Simpson: American Crime Story . Sarah Paulson in American Horror Story: Apocalypse . (FX) She also won a Golden Globe Award, a Screen Actors Guild Award, a Critics’ Choice Award and a Television Critics Association Award. She’s set to star as Aileen Wournos in the fourth instalment in Netflix and Ryan Murphy’s Monster series. Last year, Paulson won a Tony Award for her role as Toni Lafayette in the Broadway play, Appropriate . She has also starred in stage productions of The Glass Menagerie , The Cherry Orchard , Killer Joe , and Talley’s Folly . Sarah Paulson and Pedro Pascal. (Dave Benett/Getty Images) In the world of film Paulson has had memorable roles in Ocean’s 8 , Carol , and 12 Years a Slave among others. As well as having a long lasting romantic relationship with Holland Taylor , Sarah Paulson is also a close friend of Pedro Pascal . The two are often seen together, looking cute and displaying an adorable singling energy. The pair have picked up the affectionate nicknames of ‘mommy’ and ‘daddy’. And I start thinking — about everything other than the main topic of the talk. In this case, a guy was giving a sermon about the simplicity of the gospel. Don’t overcomplicate it. Master the basics. Focus on Jesus. Then he mentioned socks. Then I was lost. The “railroad lever was pulled,” and my thoughts went down a “side-track.” The speaker reminded us, about John Wooden, the legendary, former basketball coach at UCLA. He died June 4, 2010, at the age of 99. In his record setting career, he won 12 national titles, including seven national championships in a row (1967 – 1973). Famously, when new players, who were all cream of the crop recruits, arrived at UCLA, Coach Wooden would teach them how to properly put on their shoes and socks. He started with the basics. Socks had to be carefully put on, smoothed to avoid having any wrinkles. Shoes were put on with proper tightening of the laces. Vigorous pivoting and change of direction on hardwood floors is hard on feet. Avoiding blisters was the message. I’m not exactly sure what the speaker talked about next, but I was thinking about Forrest Gump. Yes, the guy in the movie of the same name played by Tom Hanks. When Forrest and Bubba arrive “in country” as soldiers in the Viet Nam, Lieutenant Dan tells them to keep their feet dry and to change their socks often. He then gives them two important pieces of advice. “Take good care of your feet and two, try not to do anything stupid!” Forrest thinks to himself, “I sure hope I don’t let him down.” Now that the seasons are changing in Sanpete, my thoughts are going to wearing heavier socks to keep my feet cozy and warm. I have lots of socks. I’m in agreement with Dumbledore when he tells Harry Potter, “One can never have enough socks.” Some years ago, my wife gave me a sort of “tower” chest of drawers for the sole purpose of storing socks. When it’s difficult to shut the drawers, I know that it’s time to start retiring some socks to make room for replacements. As a young man, while on a church mission in Norway, I made friends with a nice Lutheran family in Mo I Rana, a small city just south of the Arctic Circle. Over the course of the winter of 1972, we had many visits about religion and other topics. One evening, without saying what she was up to, Mrs. Trytti asked to be excused for a couple of minutes. She returned shortly with a bag of several pairs of socks she had pilfered from her husband’s sock supply. She had noticed that the socks I was wearing had a hole or two in them. (The custom in Norway is to remove shoes at the door upon entering a home.) I still have the pair of gifted woolen socks that are kind of the Scandinavian male equivalent of “above the knee” socks. I wear them once or twice each winter on special, cold day occasions. I consider socks as a great gift to receive. A good grade, classy, functional pair of socks is always appreciated. And since I think socks are good to receive, I consider them good to give as well. I enjoy giving socks, usually Scandinavian style ones, to family, friends, and unsuspecting acquaintances. Even though socks are traditionally the most boring gift ever, when they’re good socks, quizzical “what the heck” reactions are often transformed into, “wow, these feel good – thanks” kind of reactions. A few months ago, I read a very short, true “heart-warming” book. I borrowed it from the library. The title is “Socks for Christmas” by Andy Andrews. Andrews tells the story of how “a lousy pair of socks,” as a gift from his aunt, changed him and Christmas forever. Check it out. There are many good brands of socks out there. Aside from Nordic socks, the Stance brand is popular with me. The word “stance” suddenly has me thinking of the show “A Lot Like Love.” It’s a guilty pleasure movie of mine (a little risque’) when it comes to rom-coms. Oliver (Ashton Kutcher) asks Emily (Amanda Peet), “What’s your stance on pancakes?” She replies, “I am pro-pancakes.” So I’m wondering Sanpete, what’s your stance on socks? Where do you stand? I was thinking of going into the history of socks here, but I’ve changed my mind. Suffice it to say that the Romans are credited with inventing the first split-toe socks. These were designed for wearing with sandals. Nowadays, men, and some ladies, get made fun of for wearing socks with sandals. I say, if the socks are interesting enough, you can pull it off and get away with it. Here’s some sock trivia you may or may not want to know. The expression, “put a sock in it” means to “be quiet.” This goes back to the early “Gramophone record players” with the big horn speakers. If you wanted to reduce the volume, you “put a sock in it.” Another one. If you come to a door with a sock on the doorknob, well — that means “Do Not Disturb.” I’ve told this one for many years: “Does your nose run? Do your feet smell? If so, you must be built upside down. And finally, to finish off the socks subject. This comes from the Beatles song, “I’ve Got a Feeling.” We saw Paul McCartney perform this tune last month in Las Vegas as part of the concert encore which had a memorable “virtual duet” with John Lennon. Here’s the pertinent lyrics: “…Everybody pulled their socks up, Everybody put their foot down, oh yeah…” According to the internet, “pulling your socks up” is an English idiom meaning to pull yourself together and try hard to achieve goals and meet expectations. On Apple TV , the darkly funny crime series Your Friends & Neighbors is exactly that. The show stars Jon Hamm as a wealthy man whose once-perfect life implodes in spectacular fashion, leading to him turning to crime just to stay afloat . But this isn’t Breaking Bad , Ozark , or another “rich people behaving badly” story like The White Lotus . With a clever premise, unpredictable twists, and a surprisingly sympathetic protagonist in Hamm’s Andrew “Coop” Cooper, Your Friends & Neighbors stands apart. Apple TV has already renewed it for Season 2 , making now the perfect time to catch up on one of the smartest and funniest crime shows of the year — and the best one you’re probably not watching. What Is Apple TV\'s \'Your Friends & Neighbors\' About? In Your Friends & Neighbors , Jon Hamm plays Andrew “Coop” Cooper, a hedge-fund manager whose life self-destructs after he’s unceremoniously fired and can’t get hired anywhere else. His personal life is already in ruins after his marriage to Mel ( Amanda Peet ) collapses when he catches her in bed with his friend, retired NBA player Nick ( Mark Tallman ). That betrayal drives an even deeper wedge between Coop and his two teenage children. His on-again, off-again relationship with another neighbor, Sam ( Olivia Munn ), isn’t much better as she’s in the middle of her own messy divorce. And through it all, Coop looks after his younger sister, Ali ( Lena Hall ), a free-spirited musician who lives with mental illness. Stripped of his identity, career, and the life he once built, Coop grows desperate to maintain appearances and take care of the people he loves. Surrounded by obscene wealth in a neighborhood that feels completely insulated, he realizes how easy it would be to take the many luxury items that rich people like him had without them even realizing those very items were missing. So he starts robbing them , setting off a quiet but escalating crime spree. Coop knows he’d never be suspected, and that only makes the temptation harder to resist . In the wrong hands, a character like this could feel unlikable, but Hamm’s performance makes it easy to sympathize with him even as he spirals deeper into moral chaos. Posts By Christina Radish Jun 4, 2025 What makes Your Friends & Neighbors stand out isn’t just its premise, but the way it tells its story . It opens with Coop waking up next to a dead, bloodied body — a flash-forward that instantly hooks the audience before jumping back in time to show how he got there. The structure builds tension while charting Coop’s moral unraveling, his escalating crimes, and the dangerous secrets he uncovers about the people living around him. As the series unfolds, it becomes clear that the truths he discovers in his neighbors’ homes may be even more dangerous than his crimes . The series also benefits from an outstanding ensemble , with Hamm at the helm for a very different kind of crime drama. Jon Hamm\'s \'Your Friends & Neighbors\' Character Is Nothing Like \'Mad Men\'s Don Draper Jon Hamm\'s Coop beaten up in Your Friends & Neighbors Season 1 Image via Apple TV+ While the crime drama remains one of TV’s most reliable genres , it’s hard to stand out by simply playing it straight. What makes Your Friends & Neighbors unique is how it leans into dark comedy , even in its most dramatic moments. For Jon Hamm, this marks his first lead TV role since Mad Men , the series that made him a household name as a serious dramatic actor. But over the years, through his Saturday Night Live appearances and scene-stealing turns in comedies like Bridesmaids , Hamm has proven he’s just as gifted with humor as he is with intensity. Here, he brings both sides of his talent together. Coop may share Don Draper’s sense of regret and self-destruction , but he’s a far cry from the suave, composed ad man that defined Hamm’s career. Coop is impulsive, self-sabotaging, and often ridiculous, and Hamm isn’t afraid to lean into his vulnerability or his comedic instincts . The result is a performance that’s both deeply human and unexpectedly funny and one that turns the familiar crime-drama formula into something entirely its own. As Hamm told Collider earlier this year , the goal was never to make Coop a criminal mastermind, and that choice is exactly what makes Your Friends & Neighbors feel so refreshing . Jon Hamm\'s Crime Dramedy Series Strikes an Impressive Tonal Balance That balance of humor and darkness is also what sets the show apart tonally . After a successful first season, showrunner Jonathan Tropper also spoke about the future of Coop and his story, confirming that it won’t follow the typical antihero blueprint seen in shows like Breaking Bad . “Coop is never gonna become a criminal kingpin,” Tropper explained. “We’re not going down the Walter White road... What it is about is the risk and reward ratio — what it takes both to make him feel alive and to do what he tells himself is his exit strategy.” That difference in perspective is what gives the series its edge. Your Friends & Neighbors isn’t really about power or greed, but more a reflection of how the "1%" live and a sharp commentary on modern privilege . Coop may start out as a self-described jerk, but over time he becomes more self-aware , if not exactly redeemed. He’s got an expensive life to maintain, and in his mind, the other rich jerks he’s stealing from hardly count as victims. It’s a timely look at wealth, morality, and self-deception, which feels especially relevant in today\'s world. With Your Friends & Neighbors already renewed for Season 2 , there’s no better time to catch up. Whether you’re a longtime Jon Hamm fan, a follower of Jonathan Tropper’s work on Warrior or Banshee , or simply love a smart, character-driven crime story, this show won’t disappoint. Your Friends & Neighbors proves that even in a genre as crowded as the crime drama, there’s still room for something original, and for Hamm, it’s a reminder that his best work may be happening right now. 9 10 Your Friends and Neighbors Like Follow Followed TV-MA Drama Crime Release Date April 11, 2025 Cast See All Jon Hamm Andrew Cooper Amanda Peet Mel Cooper Where to watch Close WHERE TO WATCH Streaming Genres Drama , Crime Creator(s) Jonathan Tropper Powered by Expand Collapse Google is updating how content is shown. Wanting More Jeff Goldblum After ‘Wicked: For Good,’ Stream One of These 6 Goldblum Classic Movies By Jesse Hassenger Twitter @ rockmarooned Published Nov. 24, 2025, 4:00 p.m. ET Photos: Everett Mid-Interview Is ‘Wicked For Good’ Streaming on Netflix, Peacock or Prime Video? ‘Wicked: One Wonderful Night’ Will Leave A Handprint On Your Heart, Thanks To The Unimpeachable Vocals Of Ariana Grande and Cynthia Erivo Is ‘Independence Day’ on Netflix or Hulu? Where to Watch Will Smith’s ‘Independence Day’ For Free Wicked: For Good , the adaptation of the second act of the Broadway musical Wicked , arrived in theaters last week bearing a lot less razzle-dazzle than its predecessor. That’s by design; the second act of the show is a bit darker and more serious, full of ballad-paced and often introspective songs, and the film version adds two more on that end, leaving less room for whimsy. But one highlight in that department is “Wonderful,” a little number that centers Jeff Goldblum’s performance as, yes, the Wizard of Oz. In the song, the Wizard tries to make his case to Glinda (Ariana Grande) and Elphaba (Cynthia Erivo) that Elphaba should end her campaign against his lies, trying to recast himself as a man trying to please the populace rather than grasping for power. It’s ultimately not successful, and… that’s about it from Goldblum in the movie, even though he’s the nominal villain of the piece. He does appear occasionally throughout the film, but most of the film’s big scenes understandably involve the two marquee characters and stars at the center. In other words, despite Goldblum being well-cast in the role of a charming but unscrupulous magician-king, his fans will likely leave the Wicked experience somewhat unsatisfied, not least because these two movies are the only ones he’s made in past couple of years. He also had a crucial but largely symbolic/invisible role in Asteroid City in 2023; a variety of voiceover roles in animation; and a couple of Jurassic World movies as his signature character Ian Malcolm. He also released his third jazz album this year, featuring Grande and Erivo in guest spots! But these dribs and drabs will likely not satisfy anyone’s appetite for a tall, dark-haired, often bespectacled weirdo with distinctive, ah, speaking patterns, so with that in mind, we’ve compiled a quick overview of the best Goldblum performances with a bit more meat on their bones. Thor: Ragnarok (2017) Grandmaster Actor: Jeff Goldblum Previously In: Introduced in the pages of Avengers in 1969, Grandmaster and his cosmic scheming have been seen in cartoons ranging from the 2006 Fantastic Four show to the current Guardians of the Galaxy series. Jeff Goldblum is Jeff Goldblum, and you know who Jeff Goldblum is. In The Movie: Grandmaster is the charismatic and delightfully off-kilter mastermind behind the alien planet’s gladiator games, and-comic book Easter egg-he’s also the brother of Benicio Del Toro’s equally flamboyant character from Guardians of the Galaxy . In The Comics: This Elder of the Universe first fought the Avengers and has since pitted hero against hero in various battles for his own entertainment. Thor has never really dealt with Grandmaster on his own, but rather as part of a few Avengers lineups. Marvel Studios Later-period Goldblum – post-internet-crush, quasi-self-aware, somewhat sleazier Jeff Goldblum – was at his apex in this Marvel Cinematic Universe entry. He plays a supporting role as Grandmaster, who presides over the distant planet where Thor (Chris Hemsworth) lands and discovers his friend (“from work”) the Hulk (Mark Ruffalo) performing gladiatorial combat in an arena. Writer-director Taika Waititi has fallen somewhat out of favor since this movie’s triumphant 2017 release, but it remains both his and Thor’s best, a perfect match of sensibility and material. That includes Goldblum’s hammy, improv-accented performance. Like Waititi, he stops just short of insufferable self-consciousness, and reaches a kind of ridiculous near-perfection within his aims. Stream Thor: Ragnarok on disney+ Igby Goes Down (2002) This is another supporting role for Goldblum, essentially kicking off his 2000s-era career as a clutch supporting player, following several leading-man roles in ’90s sci-fi blockbusters. Here he plays D.H. Banes, wealthy godfather and temporary guardian of rebellious teenager Igby (Kieran Culkin), sent to stay with D.H. for the summer. Goldblum isn’t in a ton of the movie, but he’s a droll, affected delight as a philandering hypocrite, the highlight of an eclectic ensemble that also includes strong work from Amanda Peet, Bill Pullman, and Claire Danes. Stream Igby Goes Down on Tubi Deep Cover (1992) Photo: ©New Line Cinema/courtesy Everett Collection Those accustomed to seeing Goldblum in flip or campy modes might be surprised by how credible he is as a drug trafficker who forms an alliance with a cop (Laurence Fishburne) who he doesn’t realize is deep undercover, only pretending to be a fellow criminal. Actor and director Bill Duke made the rare early-’90s neo-noir that’s more of an old-fashioned crime picture than a noirish erotic thriller, and with a lot of distinctive visual style. Fishburne and Goldblum make a terrific, unexpected pairing. Stream Deep Cover on Tubi The Life Aquatic with Steve Zissou (2004) Goldblum has appeared in four Wes Anderson movies, which in AndersonWorld makes him a medium-level recurring player; more than Luke Wilson but not as many as Edward Norton. His most memorable Anderson character is also his first: Allistair Hennessey, the well-to-do nemesis of ocean-exploring filmmaker Steve Zissou (Bill Murray) in the hilarious, sad, sometimes dyspeptic The Life Aquatic . Goldblum brings his inimitable delivery to several indelible moments here: cruelly swatting and admonishing a three-legged dog; realizing he’s being rescued from the pirates he’s playing cards with and then announcing, with perfect deadpan ridiculousness, “I fold” just before getting shot by said pirates; and admitting to being “part gay, anyway” in a line penned by Anderson’s co-writer Noah Baumbach (and beloved by Anderson himself, per the film’s DVD commentary). It’s a testament to how rich a character Goldblum can play in a caricatured register with limited screen time. Where to Stream The Life Aquatic Jurassic Park (1993) If you want the sexiest and most iconic of Goldblum’s Sexy Science Nerd shtick, you have to go with the original Jurassic Park . It’s the one where he reclines, resplendent and shirtless (and also injured by an attack that eventually kills him in the book, though he’s brought back for the sequel to better match the film version), and issues dire warnings about the stupidity of playing god by bringing back dinosaurs. Said sequel The Lost World promotes him to lead (and features an iconic match-cut to his yawning face), while Independence Day really codifies his routine into shtick by pairing him with Will Smith (recall Goldblum agreeing to try an alien-defeating tactic again – “yes, this time without the oops”). This may be too much for some fans, and of course Jurassic Park is the best and least cartoony movie of the bunch. But the point is, there are a surprising number of options for seeing Goldblum save the day in a massive blockbuster. Together, these three movies grossed well over two billion dollars worldwide; add in his appearances in some later Jurassic sequels and (secondarily) his other movies, and Goldblum is one of those guys hovering around $5 billion in global grosses. Stream Jurassic Park on Peacock The Fly (1986) Photo: Everett Collection David Cronenberg’s masterpiece is also Goldblum’s peak, even as it allows him to disappear before our eyes. Goldblum’s Seth Brundle is nerdier and less swaggering than his other scientist characters, and accidentally zaps away some of his humanity when he tests a teleportation device on himself, unaware that a housefly has slipped into the device with him. Human and fly are then merged, as Brundle slowly transforms into a gigantic humanoid insect, much to the horror of his girlfriend Ronnie (Geena Davis, who had a real-life relationship with Goldblum pre-dating the film, presumably minus the… well, you’ll see). Goldblum apparently won the role in part because he was the most willing to work with the heavy prosthetics and make-up needed to portray the grotesque man-bug hybrid. That makeup won an Oscar, and many critics back in 1986 felt that Goldblum’s performance deserved a nomination, too, which he did not receive – for this movie or, as yet, any other. (At least not for acting; “Little Surprises,” a 1996 short he directed, was nominated in that category.) But his work nevertheless lives on, as part of an all-time great horror film. From the feel-good comedy Ted Lasso to the sci-fi dark mystery Severance , Apple TV covers the spectrum of tastes. The same can be said for their varied offering of crime shows. From broadly comedic whodunits to slow-burning thrillers with high stakes, Apple TV has a number of crime shows to satisfy fans of the genre. The following list covers eight of the best crime shows on Apple TV , each featuring enough murder, destruction, or robberies to keep a precinct of hardened detectives busy for the next year. 8 'Dope Thief' (2025) Brian Tyree Henry as Ray with Wagner Moura as Manny as they reel back in shock in Dope Thief. Image via Apple TV+ In Dope Thief , two friends, Ray ( Brian Tyree Henry ) and Manny ( Wagner Moura ), pose as DEA agents to rob drug houses. The plan seems like an easy enough con that won’t trace back to them, but the pair manages to draw attention from both sides of the law. In over their heads and with no one to trust, Ray and Manny will have to act carefully if they hope to survive an ordeal of their own creation. Dope Thief is beautifully shot, with cinematic visuals that make the series look more like a film than a television series. Henry and Moura’s performances are the driving force of Dope Thief , and their struggle to remain loyal to one another despite the challenges they face elevates the series past a standard crime show. Those viewers looking for a fast-paced series probably won’t find it in Dope Thief , but an audience looking for strong character work will enjoy the eight episodes. 7 'The Afterparty' (2022–2023) Ben Schwartz and Sam Richardson in The Afterparty Image via Apple TV+ The after-party of a high school reunion becomes a crime scene in the Apple murder mystery comedy The Afterparty . Pop star Xavier ( Dave Franco ) went from host to corpse in a matter of hours, and while the guests get their stories straight, the overzealous Detective Danner ( Tiffany Haddish ) sees this as a case that could make her career. Danner begins taking statements from the possible suspects, and although their stories are wildly different, a bigger picture leading to the culprit starts to form. The Afterparty is the perfect farcical murder mystery comedy ideal for fans of movies like Clue . The format of the series, where each episode is a different person’s perspective of the night’s events, avoids the trap of becoming repetitive by hiding enough clues in a story told by its reliably unreliable narrator. Each season of The Afterparty focuses on a new case with a few returning characters, but each cast is packed with comedic talent such as Sam Richardson , Zach Woods , and Ilana Glazer , making sure the improvisational-sounding flow of the comedy is consistently smooth and sharp. 6 'Smoke' (2025–Current) 'Dave Gudsen looking intently to his left in Smoke. Image via Apple TV+ Smoke follows police detective Michelle Calderone ( Jurnee Smollett ) and arson investigator Dave Gudsen ( Taron Egerton ) as they attempt to track down two serial arsonists. Gudsen balks at having Calderone assigned to his case, but soon, a mutual respect grows between the two. However, each has personal demons that factor into their investigation — demons that could likely put them on opposite sides as more details come to light. The point of view of our arsonists, the horrific damage they cause, and the enjoyment they receive from it leads to some truly creepy moments that will stick in the mind for days afterward. Egerton and Smollett play off one another well, and as their relationship continues to change over the nine episodes, we see the two investigators wordlessly switch tactics with one another, making for a compelling watch. When the plot twists in Smoke land, they drastically impact the story and guarantee the “Next Episode’ button is getting pressed. \u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b 5 'Presumed Innocent' (2024–Current) Rusty is being led away in handcuffs in court with Raymond following in Presumed Innocent. Image via Apple TV+ The murder of an assistant prosecuting attorney becomes an even bigger scandal when the Chief Deputy Prosecutor is named the prime suspect. Presumed Innocent follows Rusty Sabich ( Jake Gyllenhaal ) as he is arrested and tried for the murder of his colleague, Carolyn Polhemus ( Renate Reinsve ), with whom he was having an affair. As the court case drags shameful secrets into the light, Rusty will find it increasingly difficult to prove his innocence. Even for those familiar with the original novel of the same name by Scott Turow or the 1990 film adaptation starring Harrison Ford , the TV version of Presumed Innocent will offer new plot twists to keep viewers engaged. Gyllenhaal shines as a man grappling with guilt about his involvement with the victim , but there’s no weak link in the phenomenal cast that includes Ruth Negga as his wife, Barbara, and Bill Camp as his former boss-turned-legal counsel, Raymond Horgan. The second season of Presumed Innocent will shift the series into an anthology format with a new case to follow, but anyone looking for a quick binge will receive a complete story with Season 1. \u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b \u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b 4 'Bad Monkey' (2024–Current) Vince Vaughn sitting in a beach chair with a drink in Bad Monkey Episode 1. Image via Apple TV+ In Bad Monkey , Andrew Yancy ( Vince Vaughn ) was a great police detective who became a fairly apathetic health inspector after an altercation that put him in hot water. The arrival of a severed arm pulls Yancy back into some unofficial police work, and the fast-talking health inspector finds himself the target of some dangerous and increasingly desperate individuals. In the off chance Yancy can keep his personal life under control, he has a fighting chance of repairing his professional life if he can avoid getting killed in the process. Based on the novel of the same name by Carl Hiaasen, Bad Monkey allows its characters to be playful and get lost in banter while never losing sight of the murder mystery or the stakes of the case. Bad Monkey is the best balance of comedy and crime currently on Apple TV , and with a lead like Vaughn, who can keep one foot in both genres easily, it's a series that lends itself to substantial longevity on the streamer. The second season of Bad Monkey promises to give Yancy new co-stars to tangle with , which is one more reason to be excited for the return of the likable series. 3 'Your Friends & Neighbors' (2025–Current) A man goes from the envy of his upper-class community to the person breaking into their homes in Your Friends & Neighbors . Andrew “Coop” Cooper ( Jon Hamm ) is still emotionally reeling after the divorce from his wife, Mel ( Amanda Peet ), when he loses his job as a prominent hedge fund manager. Jaded from his recent failures and disillusioned by the wealth he sees around him, Coop begins to steal from the people he once thought of as friends. However, entering their homes allows Coop access to more than their valuables — he also discovers secrets they would kill to protect. Your Friends & Neighbors wisely relied on the charm and dry comedic ability of Hamm in the early stages of its story, but the series slowly built an interesting world around him. By the end of Season 1, many of the supporting characters were fully fleshed out into people who could carry side plots, which will only stand to make the show better. The end of Season 1 left many questions about how Coop moves forward with his life in light of major decisions, so it will be intriguing to see what his next steps are and how they impact his family, friends… and neighbors for Season 2. 2 'Criminal Record' (2024–Current) Cush Jumbo and Peter Capaldi standing beside each other in Criminal Record Image via Apple TV+ New details about an old murder case pit two detectives against one another in Criminal Record . An anonymous phone call leads Detective Sergeant June Lenker ( Cush Jumbo ) to believe an innocent man might be in jail for a murder he didn’t commit. June’s attempts to uncover the truth are blocked by Detective Chief Inspector Daniel Hegarty ( Peter Capaldi ), who believes firmly that the case in question should remain closed. When neither detective backs down, a professional disagreement quickly becomes personal. Criminal Record is one of Apple TV’s best crime offerings, loaded with the type of expertly laid out plot twists and tense drama that are the recipe for addictive television. Capaldi and Jumbo create a unique antagonistic chemistry that puts a fresh spin on a procedural mystery thriller, where the more they outmaneuver one another, the deeper their respect and will to succeed grow. With a confirmed second season of Criminal Record on the way, now is a great time to catch up before June and Daniel are back on the case. \u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b 1 'Black Bird' (2022) James in on a payphone in prison in Black Bird. Image via Apple TV+ In the intense and thrilling miniseries Black Bird , Jimmy (Taron Egerton) is a small-time crook given a once-in-a-lifetime chance to commute his 10-year sentence. The prize is great, and so is the challenge: Jimmy must befriend fellow inmate Larry Hall ( Paul Walter Hauser ) with the goal of getting a confession about suspected murders. Larry is distrustful, guards are dangerous, and Jimmy doesn’t have much time before the offer expires. Egerton takes Jimmy from arrogant to honorable with no false moments, and Hauser rightfully won an Emmy by making Larry one of the most unnerving characters on television that year. There are moments of Black Bird that become so uncomfortably tense that it’s not uncommon to feel tired after watching an episode . That’s said as the highest form of compliment, because the story continues to raise the stakes scene by scene via a masterful combination of writing and acting, making Black Bird the easiest recommendation for fans of any genre. including a character only known as 'Hot Girl' - as she's set to return to acting after eight years The Duchess of Sussex is to return to acting in the film Close Personal Friends READ MORE: Oprah gives brazen shoutout to Meghan Markle in new gift guide By MELODY FLETCHER Published: 04:55 EST, 7 November 2025 | Updated: 05:02 EST, 7 November 2025 e-mail 86 shares 532 View comments Meghan Markle is set to make a return to the world of acting, eight years after she quit the industry. The Duchess of Sussex , 44, is said to have been 'swamped with offers' for her return to the limelight, and will be playing herself in the film Close Personal Friends, with filming taking place in Pasadena in LA. But before she married Prince Harry and joined the royal family , Meghan's acting career looked very different - consisting mainly of bit parts and cameos in largely forgettable and poorly reviewed movies - and she was not nearly so in demand. Before making her name as Rachel Zane in the TV show Suits, Meghan secured minor Hollywood roles in Horrible Bosses (2011) and Remember Me (2010) - where she was typecast as a 'cute' or 'hot girl', with only seconds of screentime . Often, her cameo and pilot roles, such as her brief appearance kissing Russell Brand in Get Him To The Greek (2010) and The Boys And Girls Guide To Getting Down (2011), never actually ended up making the final cut. As a result, the now-Duchess was forced to resort to a series of raunchy roles - and was seen parading around in sexy negligee for the majority of her feature in 2012's Random Encounters - not to mention her explicit scene in the 90210 TV series . Critics, meanwhile, were less than impressed with the final results, even warning viewers that Meghan's 2006 film Deceit would 'bore them to death'. When she finally did score leading roles towards the end of her acting career, Meghan was mainly seen in repetitive and unchallenging Hallmark Movies, receiving mixed reviews at best. The mother-of-two previously told how she would get plenty of auditions but was regularly rejected by directors - which was a 'lot to chip away at your self-esteem'. Here, we give a rundown of all Meghan's film roles before meeting Prince Harry - most of which you probably won't have heard of... A Lot Like Love (2005) Meghan made her film debut in 2005, playing Natalie, the 'Hot Girl' in A Lot Like Love Meghan, then aged 24 and an unknown actress, made her big screen debut alongside Hollywood heartthrob Ashton Kutcher in the 2005 film called A Lot Like Love , where she was famously credited as 'Hot Girl.' The Duchess' very first film role was a total flop at the box office but Meghan herself, wearing a bright pink top, was only on screen for 31 seconds, and saw her attempting to flirt with Kutcher's internet entrepreneur character Oliver Martin on a flight. But she was left stunned when Oliver showed no interest because of his complicated on-off relationship with photographer Emily Friehl, Alias actress Amanda Peet. And she ended up being chatted up by business partner Jetter played by actor Kal Penn instead, who was sat across the aisle. Although she introduced herself as Natalie, she only appeared in the credits as 'Hot Girl.' The film was like an American version of One Day, where a couple met regularly over a seven-year period before falling in love. The moment was featured in Harry and Meghan's Netflix docu-series as they discussed Meghan's film career. The film received mixed reviews and a score of 40 per cent on Rotten Tomatoes, while one review in the Observer called it 'neither bad nor good enough to be anything other than utterly forgettable'. Deceit (2006) Meghan played Gwen in 2006's Deceit, again another small role for the budding actress In her second film role, Meghan again landed only a small part, playing a girl-next-door called Gwen, again appearing only in one scene. Over the kitchen table, Meghan's characeter dispensed unwanted advice to a friend caught up in a murder mystery. Her handy advice included lines such as: 'You're an investigative journalist; do what you do best - investigate her' The psychological thriller, released in 2006, followed a young man returning home after his father's death and falling in love with his best friend's wife. It explored attraction, violence, and deception. Meghan played Gwen in one scene in the film, a friend of the protagonist who offered advice to the main character. Director Matthew Cole Weiss previously revealed he'd met Prince Harry, who told him he had watched the film. The film has poor reviews online, scoring just 4.5/10 on IMDB, with viewers saying it has 'weak acting,' 'no characters' adding it will 'bore you to death'. Remember Me (2010) The Duchess did score some Hollywood roles in her film acting career, starring in Remember Me alongside Robert Pattinson In Remember Me, starring Robert Pattinson and Emilie de Ravin, Meghan had a small role as a bartender, who was aptly named Megan. She briefly interacted with Pattinson's character and only had one, three-word line: 'Do not speak', when she told his friend not to chat with her. On working with the Twilight star, Meghan recalled: 'He's a really lovely guy and a really great example to be able to watch someone who is young, who's stardom has really taken over his live in such a huge way, and yet he's still gracious, humble and cool. I think that is really endearing.' This movie marked Robert Pattinson's departure from his Twilight fame, so it would be easy to forget that a future star had a small role in the same production as well. The movie follows the story of Tyler Hawkins, who falls in love with Amy, played by Emilie de Ravin, but dies in the Twin Towers on 9/11/2001. The rom com was a financial success, grossing $56million worldwide. However, it fared less well with critics, only scoring 26 per cent on Rotten Tomatoes. The twist at the end of the show - that Pattinson's character is in his father's office in the World Trade Centre when the 9/11 attacks take place - was branded 'shockingly offensive' by Rolling Stone, and 'exploitative' by other reviewers. Meghan's real life ex-husband Trevor Engelson, was one of the film's producers, and the pair tied the knot a year later, during a party-filled celebration in Jamaica in 2011. They eventually divorced in 2014, with Meghan being linked to several men during her single years before she met now-husband Prince Harry in 2016. Get Him To The Greek (2010) Meghan Markle played Tatiana in comedy Get Him To The Greek, in which she's seen kissing comedian Russell Brand Meghan Markle played Tatiana in comedy Get Him To The Greek, in which she's seen kissing comedian Russell Brand. She reportedly had a 40-second role as a girl in a strapless metallic dress and snogged Brand's character. However, Meghan was never given a credit in the film and the scene never made it to the final cut. Is this really her? Everyone, including royal biographer Andrew Morton, says yes, reported the Mail's Jan Moir . The plot followed a record company employee, played by Jonah Hill, who went to London to get an eccentric English rock star (Russell Brand) to the Greek Theatre in Los Angeles. However, Snow is a party animal and took them on a wild ride involving alcohol and women, meeting Meghan Markle along the way. Speaking to the Evening Standard, Russell Brand said: 'She [Meghan] was in a film that I did, Get Him To The Greek it was called. 'I don't remember the film that much but I think I planted one on her. Scripted in the scene. I only know this because I think I saw a clip of it somewhere. 'They should bring that up [at the wedding]... if anyone has any reason... yeah Russell Brand snogged her in the film!' He said he didn't realise she was in it at the time as she 'wasn't married to a royal person'. The film was not panned by critics and was even said to have had its 'moments' - though Meghan's role was too short to appear in any of them. Horrible Bosses (2011) Horrible Bosses continued the trend of Meghan playing bit parts in Hollywood dark comedies Horrible Bosses in 2011 saw Meghan star alongside Jennifer Aniston and Jason Sudeikis. However, it seemed to continue the trend of her playing bit parts in Hollywood dark comedies, again having only a short cameo. The movie told the story of three employees who conspired to kill their overbearing employers. Meghan played courier driver Jamie in the comedy film and shared a few lines with Sudeikis' Kurt Buckman in another 30-second scene. In her scene, Jason Sudeikis chatted her up, saying: 'You're too cute to be a FedEx girl. You've got to be an actress or a model or something.' Her small role in the movie resurfaced after her relationship with Prince Harry became public. The film was surprisingly successful, but Meghan's role didn't attract any noticeable attention at the time. The Boys and Girls Guide to Getting Down (2011) Meghan Markle played Dana in the pilot to The Boys And Girls Guide To Getting Down, which never went anywhere Meghan Markle played Dana in The Boys And Girls Guide To Getting Down, which followed a group of friends on a night out in Los Angeles. The movie is described in the trailer as 'a film about sex drugs, booze and all around bad behaviour.' Filmed in 2011, and directed by Michael Shapiro, Meghan's character worked as a guide to Californian party-lovers, advising them on what to do and what not to do on a night out. The tongue-in-cheek movie touched on a lot of raunchy subjects, including drugs, sex and alcohol. Meghan's character Dana was seen snorting cocaine, wearing a tight black dress and obsessing about getting a boob job. The TV movie, described as a 'real life guide to sexy, drugs, and bad behavior', was filmed prior to Meghan landing her role on Suits and never went anywhere. According to IMDB, the pilot 'takes you through a night of partying in L.A.' It is described as 'funny' and 'somewhat outrageous' while offering advice to viewers on the ins and outs of partying. '[The film] gives partiers helpful tips about which substances should not be mixed, how to approach potential hook-ups, avoid undesirables [and] basically have a good time without completely destroying yourself,' the plot read on IMDB. The Candidate (2011) The Candidate, 2011: Meghan pulls strings to get a role in this hard-boiled sci-fi short film — which was produced by her then-husband, Trevor Engelson Sci-fi short film The Candidate (2011) was also produced by Meghan's then-husband, Trevor Engelson. The role was again a brief one, with Meghan starring in two scenes as Kat the secretary whose boss, Burton Grunzer, wanted to kill his incompetent colleague, Whitman Hayes. Meghan's character read her boss a latter from someone called Carl Tucker, whose text messages he repeatedly ignored. The film, by David Karlak, itself is only 19 minutes long, but received a positive reaction at the time, with one person saying it was 'better than most thrillers I've seen in theaters'. A description on the American Film Institute website reads: 'An underhanded company man is offered assistance by a secret organization that immerses him in forces beyond his control.' Dysfunctional Friends (2012) Meghan played photographer Terry in 2012's low budget film, 'Dysfunctional Friends' In the low budget film 'Dysfunctional Friends', Meghan showed she also has experience on the other side of the camera. Playing glamorous photographer Terry, Markle was seen in the little-known film shooting a handsome underwear model in a scene in scene focusing on his manhood. With flowing locks and wearing a black vest with off-the-shoulder baggy shirt, a no-nonsense Terry told male model Stylz, played by Christian Keyes: 'This is not porn. It's for the Sunday papers. This situation you have going on, it's got to get tucked in.' The images, for an underwear campaign, saw Markle's character getting increasingly frustrated with how her model was sat, before finally raging at him: 'Tuck it in!' The film followed nine friends who went their different ways after finishing college before reuniting at a rich friend's funeral. They find out that they will be eligible for a big inheritance if they stay at his mansion for five days. It bombed at the box office but paved the way for Markle to take on more serious roles. Keyes later told People Magazine that he had been 'slapped' by the 'future Queen' during filming. He explained: '[Meghan] said, 'I might improv an extra smack,' and I was like, 'smack away!' 'I knew she was going to put a little hand on it. She had some torque and rotation in the wrist.' 'It was one of her first acting gigs and she has [acting] chops, she had them back then. She was great on set. She was super cool and approachable. She was a class act.' Random Encounters (2013) Meghan had another racy role in Random Encounters, playing party girl Mindy Filmed over 18 days in 2010, the low budget romantic comedy was set in the showbusiness community in Los Angeles In Random Encounters, Meghan played Mindy, a party girl who brings home a different guy every night, and the best friend of singleton Laura, who strikes up a romance with Kevin, a man she met in a coffee shop. Filmed over 18 days in 2010, the low budget romantic comedy was set in the showbusiness community in Los Angeles. During the chick flick, which was made pre-Suits before being re-released, Mindy popped up in a host of revealing outfits including a sexy negligee before seducing a male co-star and sleeping with a cop who stopped her for a traffic offence. In one scene, Mindy could be seen showing her friend the ropes on 'the biggest dating site in LA'. She also revealed her top tips for catching a man's eye in a night club: 'Look like you're really bored and have a serious attitude problem.' When her frustrated single friend moaned that she is 'chasing a guy who doesn't insist,' Mindy replied: 'Oh honey, aren't we all.' 'It just goes to show, you just have to be in the right place at the right time. Sometimes, you only get one shot.' In one particularly racy scene Meghan was seen undressing actor Michael Rady as her character tried to make a move in a dimly-lit apartment. At other points in the film, Meghan flitted across the screen in flirty summer dresses and party frocks. Director Boris Undorf later spoke about Markle's can-do attitude while filming, reflecting: 'All the comforts of a bigger project weren't there. 'She was very much like, 'Yep, I got it. I know it's long hours, but I love doing it, and I'll do my best' to serve the film, not just myself.'' Co-star Abby Wathen (Laura) added: 'It was great to work with Meghan because she's a pro, and it's great to work with pros... It was lovely. We sat in my trailer and just giggled. She's just vivacious.' In 2018, the budget rom com was released in the UK for the first time - just two weeks before Meghan married Prince Harry. When Sparks Fly (2014) In 2014, Meghan finally landed her first major film role in Hallmark movie, When Sparks Fly Meghan's character Amy finds there's no place like how when she reunited with her high school sweetheart In 2014, Meghan finally landed a major film role, playing the lead role in the Hallmark movie, When Sparks Fly. She played Amy Peterson, a journalist who quits her small town for the big city of Chicago. She then returned to her hometown to write a human interest story about Independence Day weekend. Amy discovered that there's no place like home - and no boy like her high school sweetheart. Meghan said at the time: 'I wanted to do a romantic comedy. When the script came in, it was exactly the kind of project I wanted to be part of. 'It was light and easy and it was a departure from Rachel [Suits], who is so refined and polished. Amy Peterson is very opposite and closer to my true personality. 'It was fun to eat ribs and get barbecue sauce all over my face and run around in jeans all day.' Hallmark films all generally follow the same plot points, and while they make for comforting watching, are generally not considered 'challenging' acting roles. In 2021 alone, the channel made 41 Christmas films, with each film relatively low budget and without famous names. Anti-Social (2015) Meghan - then 35 - played American fashion model Kirsten who falls in love with Dee (Gregg Sulkin) in Anti-Social Following her relationship with Prince Harry, the film was re-released and re-edited to give Meghan a bigger role Set in England and filmed largely in Hungary, Anti-Social followed a successful street artist who was forced to jeopardise his future to help his criminal brother when gang rivalry escalates. The gangland war turned their lives upside down, bringing the attention of the police as well as other criminals. The low-budget British coming-of-age story was inspired by a number of real-life smash-and-grab raids across London from 2009 to 2013. Again, the Duchess was chosen to play the female lead and it even co-starred grime star Skepta. Meghan - then 35 - played American fashion model Kirsten who falls in love with Dee (Gregg Sulkin), a talented Banksy-esque street-artist who was sucked into crime. One of her lines included: 'I know you have had to climb a mountain to get away from this crap and see life for what it can be. You inspire me.' Following her relationship with Prince Harry, the film was re-released and re-edited to give Meghan a bigger role as bosses sought to capitalise on her new royal links. Originally, it had been shown at just 40 screens in the UK when it was released in 2015. Speaking of the decision to re-release it, Director Reg Traviss - who had dated Amy Winehouse before she died - said he wanted to 'delve deeper into one of the storylines with.. a shorter, more compact version of the original'. In the three-minute trailer, Meghan's character was shown modelling perfume, emerging from a shower and drinking champagne at a number of West End nightclubs. She was heard saying: 'I'm going to go and see my boyfriend, he's an artist. A street artist.' In a scene which showed shoot-outs in London, depicting Marcus and his cool friends getting pulled into a dangerous gang war, she said: 'I hate violence... I'm from a sleepy little beach town, I'm just not used to this.' Upon its release, the film generally received negative reviews, with one critic calling the film a 'painful slog'. In The Observer, critic Mark Kermode awarded it two stars, calling it an 'uninspiring crime caper' that 'sits awkwardly alongside dreary discussions of the politics of street art'. Dater's Handbook (2016) Meghan's final film role saw her play Cassandra Barber in 2016's Dater's Handbook Cass soon realised that there was no rule book to love, binned her manual and met the man of her dreams In Meghan's final film role before quitting the industry upon joining the Royal Family, she played another lead role for the Hallmark Channel, in 2016's Dater's Handbook. The romantic movie centred around Cassandra Barber, who realised she had a recurring habit of picking the wrong type of guy, turning to relationship expert, Dr. Susie, and her latest self-help book, The Dater's Handbook to help with her ailing love life. 'Of course I wanna get married,' Meghan's character Cass told her mother. 'I've got to change how I choose relationships.' She followed the advice in Dr. Susie's book to evaluate potential suitors, and was forced to choose between reliable George (Jonathan Scarfe) and fun-loving Robert (Kristoffer Polaha). Cass soon realised that there was no rule book to love, binned her manual and met the man of her dreams. Little did Meghan know that six months later she'd meet her real-life prince. Successful career women, both Cassandra and Meghan were set up with their dream suitor by a mutual pal, bonding on and off-screen with their respective suitors over their shared love of animals and the great outdoors. Additionally, Meghan and her character were whisked away on sporty dates by their suitors - while Cass' mother joined the pair at a concert in the movie, Harry flew Meghan's mother Doria to the Invictus Games in Toronto in real life. Many joked at the time of the movie's release that while the character she played on screen had been unlucky in love, Meghan's real love life was very different. During the film's press tour, Meghan said: 'At the end of the day, when it comes down to finding the person that you're right for, that's not the person you're going to play games with. 'I think following her heart has really ended up proving to work out well for Cass, and I think for a lot of women watching this, I would give them that same advice.' The film, a classic Hallmark movie, was branded 'predictable and simple' by critics. On IMDB, one reviewer even said: 'The story was silly, the acting was below average, and the actors had no chemistry.'
